correctness.rationale: From the verified published coefficient identity, direct algebra gives y2=F/(3+2k-k^2+2z). The derivative bound uses the exact maximizer of e^-z(kz-1-k+k^2) and the strictly negative logarithmic inequality. Thus each k has precisely one positive zero. The quadratic F=A+Bk+Ck² is strictly concave in k; its interior vertex is proved using B>0 and B+2C<0. Pointwise strict decrease in z makes the maximal envelope strictly decreasing; sign brackets at log4 and 2 yield one and only one tangency root D(z)=0 and unique global k optimizer. The BDF2 crossing follows from exact factorization at log4. Rational consistency checks, recurrence checks, 1,001 parameter-grid sign boundaries and high-precision root diagnostics were run from the actual standalone package, and no finite check is treated as proof.

The source derives coefficients and damping/error tradeoff but does not give this one-update frontier. value.rationale: The parameter-specific exact first-update sign frontier is a natural finite-horizon invariant for an error-optimized stiff integrator: a one-step positive diagnostic is weaker than persistent positive trajectory safety. The unique first-step optimizer is quantitatively different from the published best persistent-positivity parameter and the complete crossing criterion identifies when increasing the damping parameter makes the first output worse than classical BDF2. At k=0.8, one apparently positive completed output remains possible near z=1.38 although the indexed robust positivity boundary is only z=0.45. This exact benchmark can inform short-horizon diagnostic design and caution against extrapolating a single accepted update; it is not a global scheme improvement or a broad PDE guarantee.
